summary.headline: HoloLens update-ring wording refreshed
summary.summary: The update rings article made a minor wording change to the statement that Windows Holographic for Business supports a subset of Windows update settings.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change; verify HoloLens settings against the documented supported subset.

summary.headline: Company Portal manual download switches to winget download
summary.summary: The manual Company Portal article now uses `winget download "Company Portal" --source msstore` rather than the install command, and identifies the default Downloads folder.
summary.adminImpact: Use winget download when obtaining the offline Company Portal package and dependencies for manual upload.

summary.headline: Company Portal winget download steps reformatted
summary.summary: The Company Portal download command was indented as a PowerShell block and the Downloads-folder guidance was converted from a note to regular text.
summary.adminImpact: No workflow change; use `--download-directory` when a custom download location is needed.

summary.headline: MDT retirement warning added to release notes
summary.summary: The release notes now state that Microsoft Deployment Toolkit and its Configuration Manager integration are retired and unsupported, warn that retained MDT task-sequence steps can cause corruption or modification failures, and point to Autopilot or supported OSD.
summary.adminImpact: Remove MDT task-sequence steps and MDT integration, then plan a move to Autopilot or supported Configuration Manager OSD.

summary.headline: MDT retirement action wording clarified
summary.summary: The MDT retirement warning changed the instruction to say customers should remove MDT task-sequence steps and MDT integration to avoid corruption and modification failures.
summary.adminImpact: Treat removal of MDT integration as the documented migration action.

summary.headline: Apple settings catalog update listed as in development
summary.summary: The in-development page says Apple’s Rapid Security Responses rebrand to Background Security Improvements will be reflected in iOS/iPadOS Settings Catalog restrictions, and changes Android management-mode filtering to future tense.
summary.adminImpact: Treat the Apple label update and Android filter as planned; review relevant settings catalog policies when available.

summary.headline: EPM FAQ adds supported virtual-device guidance
summary.summary: The EPM FAQ replaces the statement that Azure Virtual Desktop is unsupported with a supported-virtual-devices section and clarifies that administrator launches matching elevation rules are reported as unmanaged elevations.
summary.adminImpact: Review the supported virtual-device list before onboarding virtual desktops to Endpoint Privilege Management.

summary.headline: EPM planning guidance adds AVD single-session support
summary.summary: The EPM planning article now states that EPM policies support Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs instead of listing Azure Virtual Desktop as unsupported.
summary.adminImpact: Validate that AVD deployments are single-session VMs before assigning EPM policies.

summary.headline: EPM virtual-platform support made explicit
summary.summary: The EPM plan replaced a support note with a dedicated statement that Endpoint Privilege Management supports specified virtual platforms.
summary.adminImpact: Use the virtual-platform support section to validate Windows 365 or Azure Virtual Desktop scope before rollout.

summary.headline: Feature update advanced licensing links to Autopatch entitlement
summary.summary: The article replaced a hard-coded list of qualifying Windows licenses with a link to the Autopatch entitlement licensing documentation for gradual rollout and optional feature updates.
summary.adminImpact: Validate advanced feature-update licensing against the linked Autopatch entitlement requirements.

summary.headline: Windows update registered-device limitations clarified
summary.summary: The overview renames the Workplace Joined limitation section for Microsoft Entra registered devices and states that feature, quality, driver, and Hotpatch policies relying on WUfB DS cannot be used on those devices.
summary.adminImpact: Use Windows Update client policies and update rings for Microsoft Entra registered devices; do not target them with WUfB DS-backed policy types.

summary.headline: Update rings requirements wording refreshed
summary.summary: The update rings article clarifies that Intune Plan 1 is required for core policy creation and assignment and updates platform and edition wording.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm Intune Plan 1 licensing before creating or assigning update ring policies.

summary.headline: Registered-device restrictions moved into prerequisites
summary.summary: The Windows updates overview moves Microsoft Entra registered-device restrictions into its general prerequisites: WUfB DS-backed feature, quality, driver, and Hotpatch policies are unsupported, while update rings remain available.
summary.adminImpact: Check device join type before choosing a Windows update policy type.

summary.headline: Registered-device limitation formatting corrected
summary.summary: The registered-device limitation sentence received a formatting-only correction.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change; retain the documented restriction on WUfB DS-backed policy types.

summary.headline: Driver report prerequisites reorganized
summary.summary: The driver reports article reorganized prerequisites into shared device and tenant requirement sections and states Windows diagnostic data must be collected at Required or higher for complete status and event reporting.
summary.adminImpact: Enable Required-or-higher Windows diagnostic data collection and verify tenant prerequisites before relying on driver update reports.

summary.headline: Expedited update report procedure renumbered
summary.summary: The expedited quality update reporting steps were renumbered using Markdown auto-numbering without changing the report navigation or actions.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change; continue using Reports > Windows updates and the Windows Expedited Update Report.

summary.headline: Feature update prerequisites remove report-only data collection
summary.summary: The feature update policy prerequisites removed the instruction to enable data collection for reporting.
summary.adminImpact: Configure diagnostic data according to the reporting documentation when reports are needed, rather than treating it as a deployment prerequisite.

summary.headline: Update rings management heading simplified
summary.summary: The article heading changed from Manage your Windows Update rings to Manage update rings.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change.

summary.headline: Driver reporting prerequisites clarify data-sharing scope
summary.summary: The report requirements now separate tenant configuration from device configuration and direct admins to enable Windows diagnostic data at Required or higher for driver-update reporting.
summary.adminImpact: Ensure Windows diagnostic data is shared with Intune at Required or higher on devices included in driver update reports.

summary.headline: Feature update reporting prerequisites reorganized
summary.summary: The feature update reports article reorganized diagnostic-data requirements into tenant and device sections, explains that Windows update reports require sharing diagnostic data with Intune, and removes older duplicate collection text.
summary.adminImpact: Enable Windows diagnostic-data sharing with Intune for device-based feature update reporting.

summary.headline: Quality update reports whitespace cleaned up
summary.summary: The quality update reports article removed blank lines only.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change.

summary.headline: Driver updates FAQ moved to separate article
summary.summary: The driver updates overview removed its Frequently Asked Questions section, including assignment filters, Autopilot, rollback, policy conflict, pauses, deadlines, deferrals, and co-management guidance, following publication of a separate FAQ article.
summary.adminImpact: Use driver-updates-faqs.md for operational questions about driver update policies.

summary.headline: Windows Driver updates overview article restored
summary.summary: A complete Windows Driver update management overview was added, documenting approvals, pauses, prerequisites, supported editions, cloud limitations, RBAC, deployment planning, and reporting.
summary.adminImpact: Review the overview before deploying driver policies and confirm licensing, platform, network, and role requirements.

summary.headline: Audit retention wording corrected
summary.summary: The privacy article corrects the audit-log retention phrase to two years.
summary.adminImpact: No change beyond the previously documented two-year retention period.

summary.headline: Driver policy article refreshes setup guidance
summary.summary: The driver policy article is retitled Manage Windows driver update policies, adds a Before you begin section linking overview requirements, and clarifies that admins can create, approve, deploy, and pause individual driver updates.
summary.adminImpact: Review the overview prerequisites before creating a driver policy and plan regular review of newly available drivers.
